doc.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Why jazz declined after the 1960s: Coltrane's death and Miles leaving
summary: Coltrane died in 1967 and Miles stopped playing jazz around 1968-69, leaving a void for younger players.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Forties, fifties, even the sixties. The sixties was when it started to decline, you know. But in the forties and fifties, thirties, forties, fifties….
When in the sixties do you mark this decline?

I think it was like a confluence of events. Old guys started dying. Trane died, too soon. And then Miles stopped playing jazz. And all the young guys, who were looking up to him, he didn’t have any faith in the music, so they didn’t have any faith in the music. So they

split. And then there was just this big void where you had guys from the fifties continuing to play gigs, but not updating the culture - the way that culture gets updated by subsequent generations. And that was kinda where it fell into a sink hole.
So Trane dies in sixty-seven, Miles stops playing jazz in….
It was done. It was just….
